articles.title: Home Assistant cuts the wait before voice replies begin
articles.dek: Streaming speech bypasses a conversion delay, helping Wyoming and Home Assistant Cloud replies start sooner.
body: Home Assistant changes how it converts streaming speech for voice satellites, letting replies begin without waiting for most of the message to arrive. The change applies to streaming speech from Wyoming and Home Assistant Cloud when the audio needs conversion.

In Michael Hansen’s simulated three-second utterance, generated at just above speaking speed, the first converted audio arrived after 0.10 seconds instead of 2.90. These are the best of three runs at the conversion stage, rather than the full time between a spoken request and its answer.
Hansen reads the incoming audio format first and passes its samples directly to the converter, avoiding the wait for it to inspect the stream. Complete audio files retain their existing handling.

pullRequests.title: Stream TTS audio to ffmpeg as raw PCM samples

articles.title: ESPHome keeps firmware updates moving through unreliable Wi-Fi
articles.dek: Automatic retries take a different route when packet loss defeats the ordinary upload, with no new setting to configure.
body: ESPHome gives devices on unreliable Wi-Fi a better chance of completing a wireless firmware update without being carried closer to the router. The uploader switches its data transfer automatically when the connection shows packet loss, while clean connections keep the existing path.

In J. Nick Koston’s test with an ESP32 beside the uploading computer and 65% packet loss deliberately introduced in both directions, the old transfer failed every time. The new transfer completed the upload in about three and a half minutes; connection setup brought the complete process to roughly eight to twelve minutes. ESP8266 uploads also completed under the same simulated loss.

The change keeps the existing authentication and image checks, and encrypted uploads retain their encryption. Both the uploader and the device need support for the new transfer; older devices remain compatible through the ordinary method, and a blocked alternative port falls back to it.

pullRequests.title: [ota] Fall back to a UDP data phase when the link is lossy
[ota] Document the UDP upload for unreliable Wi-Fi

articles.title: ESPHome detects presence in zones shaped around a room
articles.dek: LD2450 sensors detect occupied areas at radar speed, without sending every position update to Home Assistant.
body: ESPHome lets an LD2450 presence sensor follow an irregularly shaped part of a room, such as a seating or desk area, instead of limiting each zone to a rectangle. The device evaluates the polygon itself and sends a presence change to Home Assistant when it happens.

The calculations run at the radar’s ten updates per second. Compared with calculating zones in Home Assistant from the usual once-a-second position reports, this avoids roughly nine-tenths of a second of added detection delay without sending every position update across the network.

Fabio Pugliese Ornellas tested the feature for several days on hardware using his companion dashboard card to draw the zones. Each zone exposes its outline and an occupied-or-empty reading; the drawing card is a separate project.

articles.title: Home Assistant shows an integration’s logs as problems happen
articles.dek: A focused live view lets people reproduce an issue without searching the whole system log.
body: Home Assistant adds a live log view to each integration’s page while debug logging is enabled. It includes that integration and the libraries it uses, showing captured lines from the current Home Assistant session and new ones as they arrive.

The dialog can search the text, wrap long lines and download its captured output. Scrolling back pauses following the newest lines, with a control to jump forward again. The banner also explains that turning debug logging off downloads the log.

pullRequests.title: Add live log dialog to integration page
Explain debug logging banner and make disable the main action

articles.title: ESPHome controls Midea PortaSplit air conditioners locally
articles.dek: A dedicated wired connection supplies climate controls that the existing Midea component cannot provide.
body: ESPHome adds a dedicated connection for the Midea PortaSplit air conditioner, using a serial link in place of its original Wi-Fi module. It controls the operating mode, target temperature, five fan speeds and vertical swing, together with sleep, boost, eco and frost-protection presets.

The PortaSplit uses a different command protocol from the existing Midea component. The new connection reads back the result after each command and answers the appliance’s checks for its original module. Contributor Fexiven verified it against a real unit and supplies the companion guide in their first contribution to ESPHome’s documentation.
The connection covers climate controls. Extra sensor and adjustment entities remain separate follow-up work.

pullRequests.title: [midea_portasplit] Add Midea PortaSplit climate component
[midea_portasplit] Add Midea PortaSplit climate documentation

articles.title: Home Assistant disconnects users when their accounts are removed
articles.dek: Deleting an administrator account stops its existing connection from continuing to send commands.
body: Home Assistant closes an access gap when an account is deleted. Previously, the account’s existing live connections could keep working; a removed administrator could continue sending administrator commands for as long as the connection stayed open.
Frenck makes account removal revoke its access tokens through the same connection-closing behavior already used when deactivating an account.

pullRequests.title: Revoke refresh tokens when removing a user

articles.title: Music Assistant eases Apple Music’s shared request limits
articles.dek: Unchanged libraries skip full scans, while background retries stop holding up browsing.
body: Music Assistant cuts unnecessary Apple Music requests so background library work puts less pressure on listening and browsing. Apple limits requests across the developer account used by Music Assistant installations, making avoidable traffic a shared problem.

Library synchronization moves from twice a day to daily for installations still using the old default. A small check skips an unchanged library, with a full scan at least weekly and manual scans always available. Favorites still receive a daily check; playlist tracks are fetched again when their change marker changes instead of on every expired page cache.

During rate limiting, background requests give up after three attempts while playback and ordinary user actions retain eight. This reduces time spent waiting behind background work. Some tasks started by a person, including playlist imports, also use that shorter retry limit. Custom synchronization schedules are preserved.

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps Audiobookshelf access tokens out of media links
articles.dek: Existing saved artwork addresses are cleaned, with a compatibility cost for older servers.
body: Music Assistant keeps the Audiobookshelf access token on the server instead of handing it out in audio and artwork links. Audio passes through Music Assistant, and a library migration removes tokens from image addresses already saved in the library, listening log and play history.

The connection also exchanges completed and played states more reliably with Audiobookshelf, including changes made in its web interface during an open listening session. Servers older than Audiobookshelf 2.17.0 lose cover images because those versions require the token in the image address.

pullRequests.title: Optimize the Audiobookshelf progress sync and keep its token on the server

articles.title: ESPHome joins Wi-Fi through a scanned setup code
articles.dek: Compatible phones can supply network credentials to an ESP32 using Wi-Fi Easy Connect.
body: ESPHome adds Wi-Fi Easy Connect setup for ESP32 devices: the device supplies a QR-code payload, and a compatible phone scans it to send the network credentials. Makers can display the code through an ESPHome automation instead of requiring someone to type credentials into a fallback web page.

The device saves the network for later restarts and uses ESPHome’s ordinary connection and retry handling. Setup starts when no network is configured, or after configured networks fail for a chosen timeout. A Pixel phone successfully set up an ESP32-S3 in testing, but failed to complete setup on a classic ESP32; phone and chip compatibility matters.

articles.title: Sonoff plug fixes make small electrical loads visible
articles.dek: A Zigbee firmware update repairs readings below 110 watts, while ESPHome stops a separate metering chip repeatedly reporting false zeroes.
body: Two changes improve low-power measurements on Sonoff plugs. Firmware 2.1.3 for the Zigbee S60ZBTPF and S60ZBTPG enters Zigpy’s update collection with a fix for incorrect voltage, power and energy values below 110 watts.

Separately, ESPHome’s CSE7766-family metering driver keeps the last valid reading while a low-power load waits for its next measurement. On a tested Sonoff S60TPF, a 2.2-watt lamp previously appeared as zero in 75 of 79 reports. Keeping the measurement prevents a running small appliance from repeatedly looking switched off.

The ESPHome correction has a trade-off: after a small load actually switches off, zero can take a few seconds to appear, and up to about sixteen seconds for the smallest tested range. Higher loads keep their existing response, and the energy counter is unchanged. These are separate fixes for different hardware and software paths.

articles.title: Music Assistant shows when a play request is still working
articles.dek: Repeated taps stop piling up, and leaving the page no longer cancels the request.
body: Music Assistant’s mobile app keeps a play request running when someone leaves the screen and shows a progress ring while the music is being prepared. The indicator also reflects requests started from another phone, the web interface or a car connection.

Andrii Mitnovych makes identical double taps count once. If several different play requests are waiting, the newest replaces an older waiting choice; requests to add music or play it next keep their order. The play control remains usable while the ring is showing.

articles.title: Home Assistant caps the power used by compatible Daikin units
articles.dek: Automations can lower the demand limit during expensive electricity periods.
body: Home Assistant adds a demand-control action for compatible Daikin air conditioners. An automation can limit the unit’s maximum power to a percentage of its nominal power, including during periods of high electricity prices.
The action checks the capability reported by the unit and reports an error on models without demand control. It is an automation action, rather than an additional dashboard control entity.

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps MQTT devices when one component is removed
articles.dek: Deleting a single discovered entity stops clearing the rest of its device.
body: Home Assistant prevents the removal of one MQTT-discovered entity from erasing all the other components of its device. The correction also protects devices when software cleans up old discovery messages after changing how it describes the device.

A device remains while it has supported enabled or disabled components. Removing the entire device still clears it; removing only an entity in Home Assistant can allow it to return when the device publishes its configuration again. To keep that component away, disable it or remove it from the device’s discovery configuration.

articles.title: Music Assistant opens large collections beyond the first 500 items
articles.dek: New server paging reaches the rest of artist collections and service folders; clients must adopt it.
body: Music Assistant removes the 500-item cutoff from the library portions of artist pages and music-service browse folders. Larger collections can be read in pages, with the server handling search and order instead of requiring every client to load and arrange the whole list.

The paging interface also covers playlists, podcast episodes, genres and alternate versions, with search and sorting handled by the server. Most assembled lists are cached for fifteen minutes; a manual refresh picks up outside changes immediately. Client applications need to adopt the interface to reach every item, while older clients receive the first page.

body: Home Assistant’s Android app hides its contents in the recent-apps view when the app is locked. Previously, the system preview could still show the last dashboard, exposing its contents without opening the locked app.

articles.title: Home Assistant gives helper values the right measurement types
articles.dek: Manual numbers can convert units, while calculated totals can identify water, gas and money.
body: Home Assistant adds measurement types to number helpers, allowing a manually entered temperature or other supported value to behave like a measured number. The value and its limits follow the chosen display unit, and setting a value converts it back to the helper’s saved unit.

The helper form filters units to match the selected type. Integral helpers, which turn a rate into a running total, also gain a type setting: water or gas volume and monetary totals can carry the appropriate meaning rather than relying only on the existing power-to-energy inference.

An integral helper uses the chosen type only when its units and statistics are compatible; otherwise it keeps its existing inference and warns about the mismatch. Tom Carpenter supplies the integral-helper change in his first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

articles.title: Assist understands more Brazilian Portuguese list and volume requests
articles.dek: Shopping-list commands stop mistaking part of the instruction for the item name.
body: Assist recognizes more everyday Brazilian Portuguese requests for shopping lists and sound volume. A request to mark milk as completed no longer treats “as completed” as part of the item’s name, and phrases referring to “my shopping list” match correctly.

The command grammar adds forms such as “já comprei leite” for a bought item and accepts “som” alongside “volume” when changing the sound level. LFonzie supplies the changes, beginning with their first contribution to the intents repository.
